summary.headline: Laxmi India Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~70% YoY to INR16.4 crore, NIM expanded to 11.36%, while credit cost jumped to 0.95% on vehicle loans.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong growth: AUM up 28% YoY to INR1,721.7 crore, own book up 31.7% to INR1,626.9 crore, and disbursements of INR232 crore versus INR166 crore a year ago. Profitability improved sharply, with PBT up ~72% to INR21.9 crore and PAT up ~70% to INR16.4 crore, driven by a 67 bps fall in cost of borrowing to 10.66%. Asset quality improved sequentially (GNPA 2.08%, NNPA 0.93%), but credit cost rose to INR3.69 crore (0.95%) from 0.58%, attributed mainly to vehicle finance and an extra 10% provisioning on up-money cases. Management kept FY27 PAT growth guidance of 40-45% and AUM growth of 30-35% unchanged.

segments.name: MSME (secured SME)
segments.commentary: Core vertical at ~INR1,395 crore AUM; management says core MSME and construction credit costs remain moderate. A new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets was recently launched.

segments.name: Vehicle finance (wheels)
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR131 crore; source of the credit cost rise, attributed to older vintages in specific geographies. Acceptance criteria tightened and field follow-ups increased.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth target of ~30-35% annually maintained.
FY27 PAT growth guidance of ~40-45% maintained; Q1 PAT growth stated to be significantly ahead of this range, with revision to be considered after the next few quarters.
Targeted ROA of 3.5-3.75% by year-end, per analyst question and management reply.
Further 20-25 bps reduction in cost of borrowing expected over coming quarters, assuming stable global rates and no RBI hike.
Cost-to-income ratio currently below 50%; internal target ~42-44%.
Plan to add 30-35 branches across existing states in FY27; 10 added in Q1. One or two new states planned per year.
Capital raise of ~INR300-350 crore planned in roughly 1-1.5 years (start of next financial year), when leverage reaches ~3.5-4x (pre-IPO level ~4-4.5x).
capex_capacity: Branch network at 184 across six states (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra); 25 branches added over the last year, including 10 in UP and 6 in Maharashtra.
New branches reach breakeven in ~7-9 months (range 5-12 months) at an AUM of ~INR1.5-2 crore per branch; one of the 25 new branches is already at breakeven.
Branches are tiered: Tier 1 with 5-6 relationship officers, Tier 2 with 5-6, Tier 3 with 2-5.
Rajasthan (mother state, ~90 branches) remains the largest contributor; other states are expected to gain share over 3-4 years.
Digitised LOS/LMS, CKYC, RCU, eNACH and auto-dialer; only physical loan signing remains, expected to move to eSign shortly.
demand_pricing: Disbursements of INR232 crore grew ~40% YoY, ahead of 28% AUM growth; management attributes the gap to repayments and closures.
Portfolio yield broadly stable at 21.67%; NIM gain came from lower funding cost, not yield.
Management said it may pass on borrowing-cost relief to borrowers depending on asset quality and board decision.
37% of borrowers are first-time borrowers; customer base at ~43,946 vs 37,122 a year ago.
Management flagged rising competitive intensity in MSME lending and said underwriting discipline will be maintained.
